findings.summary: crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The gate change is outside the listed deliverables, but the plan needs it and gives its reason.
findings.evidence: invariant.rs:149-157 sends records-only commits to names_existing_work (799-831). That function accepts only Athena-Job, Athena-Intervention or Athena-Record trailers. intervention() (760-774) requires an Athena-Intervention trailer. So stripping trailers without changing the gate makes Committer::build_commit_in (commits.rs:172) refuse its own commit. Athena's finding 1 flags the same file. Fix: Keep the change. Name invariant.rs in the change description as a scope addition the trailer stop needs.

findings.summary: After C0, a commit that adds any intervention record would be accepted as a declared intervention.
findings.evidence: added_interventions (invariant.rs:778-796) only matches the path shape. Today the trailer and the added record must agree (intervention(), 760-774). Without the trailer, that cross-check is gone. Fix: Add a gate test showing that a governed change plus an unrelated or malformed intervention record is still refused. Or limit the rule to an id the commit adds whose record parses as a well-formed intervention.

findings.summary: "Add a core CutoverSpec" means building a new value of the existing type, not defining a new type.
findings.evidence: test_support.rs:85 already defines `pub struct CutoverSpec<'a>`, and CutoverFixture::build(spec) is at line 385. Fix: Reword it as: build a CutoverSpec value (capability and scripts) for the existing type.

findings.summary: The plan does not say why the other commit_tree callers are out of scope.
findings.evidence: commit_tree callers: run.rs:1807 (the 'Candidate for job' message, no trailers), land.rs:451, pr.rs:589 and gh.rs:5256 (tests), and records_branch.rs:366 (its messages contain no Athena- text; grep found none). Fix: Add a sentence to the D111 addendum saying these writers carry no Athena- trailers, so build_commit_in covers every commit that does.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot, and it holds up. Committer::build_commit_in (commits.rs:150-185) is the shared place where Athena builds commits, and it runs the gate on the commit it makes, so stripping trailers there needs the gate change the plan pairs with it. The gate's landing path already works from content: Athena-Verified-Content and Athena-Job are only hints that must agree (invariant.rs:363-400). Only the intervention and records-only paths depend on trailers, and those are the two places Decision 2 changes. attribution.rs says it never reads commit messages. retry_landing (run.rs:2785-2798) bails with 'closing commit ... was not found' when no Athena-Job trailer is present, so the criterion-2 test would fail without the post-C0 branch. The auditor test in a fresh clone, paired with the old trailer-only lookup, is a real failing-then-passing proof. The other named functions exist: cutover_job_for (gh.rs:1680), squash_text (athena-git lib.rs:715), cutover_commit (attribution.rs:83), read_changed_files (auditor.rs:168), trace (status.rs:816) and CutoverFixture::build (test_support.rs:385). A grep of docs/ found no 'retry_landing has no test' text, and the plan handles that case. The findings are minor: the gate is a justified addition to the scope, the intervention content rule should get a negative test, and two wording points. Verdict: accept.
